about: Test questions for the Med-QUEST chatbot. Each expected answer comes from the page named in 'source' on medquest.hawaii.gov (pulled 2026-11-18). 'must' is a list of facts the answer has to contain; each fact is a list of acceptable wordings. 'links' are pages or files the answer should point to. 'call_ok' marks questions where telling the person to call is a correct part of the answer; anywhere else a phone referral counts as unneeded. Edit freely: add real users' questions here.

turns: How do I apply for Medicaid?
questions.reference: Three ways: online at medical.mybenefits.hawaii.gov, by phone at 1-800-316-8005, or on paper with Form DHS 1100 mailed or faxed to an eligibility office.

turns: Where do I apply for Medicaid?
questions.reference: Online, by phone, or with the paper Form DHS 1100. Should offer the Form 1100 download and the Apply for Medicaid page.

turns: Can I apply on paper? What form do I use?
questions.reference: Yes: fill out Form DHS 1100, print it, and mail or fax it to the nearest Med-QUEST eligibility office.

turns: Can I apply online?
questions.reference: Yes, at medical.mybenefits.hawaii.gov (the KOLEA portal), which is the fastest way.

turns: I have a disability. Which forms do I need to apply?
questions.reference: DHS 1100 plus DHS 1100B, DHS 1127 and DHS 1128.

turns: My mom needs long-term care. What forms does she need to apply?
questions.reference: DHS 1100, DHS 1100B, DHS 1167, DHS 1169, DHS 1169A, DHS 8003 and DHS 8004.

turns: how do i aply for medicad
questions.reference: Same as 'How do I apply': online, phone, or paper.

turns: How do I renew my coverage?
questions.reference: Online at the Med-QUEST portal (fastest), with the paper form that came with the pink renewal notice, or by phone at 1-800-316-8005.

turns: How will I know when it's time to renew?
questions.reference: Med-QUEST sends a pink letter, a text message, an email, or all three. Some people are renewed automatically.

turns: Do I have to renew every year?
questions.reference: Yes. Med-QUEST reviews your information every year; some people are renewed automatically.

turns: I forgot to renew and my coverage stopped. What do I do?
questions.reference: Within 90 days of the renewal date you can still complete the renewal and get coverage reinstated; after 90 days, apply again.

turns: How do I report a change of address?
questions.reference: Through your KOLEA portal account, with Form DHS 1179A (Change of Circumstance Report) sent to your island's eligibility office, or by phone at 1-800-316-8005.

turns: I got a new job and my income changed. Do I need to tell anyone?
questions.reference: Yes, contact Med-QUEST when you get or change jobs or your income changes: KOLEA portal, Form DHS 1179A, or 1-800-316-8005.

turns: I just had a baby. Is my baby covered?
questions.reference: If you were enrolled in a QUEST Integration plan when you delivered, your newborn is automatically enrolled in your plan for at least 30 days. Report the birth to Med-QUEST.

turns: What health plans can I choose from?
questions.reference: Five: AlohaCare, HMSA, Kaiser Permanente, 'Ohana Health Plan, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan.

turns: How do I change my health plan?
questions.reference: Within 15 days of your enrollment choice notice, or at any time after 12 months in your current plan, or during the annual plan change period. Call Med-QUEST Customer Service.

turns: What happens if I don't pick a health plan?
questions.reference: Med-QUEST assigns one to you. If you stay with it you don't need to do anything.

turns: If I switch plans, when does the new plan start?
must: first day of the following month
first day of the next month
questions.reference: On the first day of the following month.

turns: What is the phone number for Kaiser's QUEST plan?
I lost my Medicaid card, how do I get a new one?
questions.reference: Call Med-QUEST at 1-800-316-8005 to replace a lost Medicaid ID card; for a lost health plan member card, contact your health plan.

turns: How do I choose a primary care doctor?
questions.reference: Your health plan's welcome packet has a form to choose a PCP. You have 15 days from the enrollment start date; otherwise the plan assigns one. You can change your PCP at any time.

turns: I need to see a doctor but I haven't gotten my ID card yet. What do I do?
questions.reference: Take the enrollment notice you got in the mail to your doctor; it works until your ID card arrives.

turns: Does Med-QUEST cover dental for adults?
questions.reference: Yes. Age 21 and older: preventive, diagnostic and radiology, endodontic, restorative, oral surgery, periodontal, prosthodontic, and emergency and palliative treatment.

turns: How do I find a dentist that takes Medicaid?
questions.reference: Call Community Case Management Corp (CCMC): O'ahu 808-792-1070, neighbor islands 1-888-792-1070.

turns: Can Medicaid pay for rides to my doctor appointments?
questions.reference: Yes, Non-Emergency Medical Transportation: a free ride to medically necessary appointments when you have no other way to get there, arranged through your health plan with prior approval. Not for emergencies (call 911).

turns: Does Med-QUEST cover eye exams and glasses?
questions.reference: Vision and hearing services are covered benefits, and durable medical equipment includes visual appliances. Check with your health plan for details.

turns: Are prescription drugs covered?
questions.reference: Yes, prescription drugs are a covered QUEST Integration benefit.

turns: Does Med-QUEST cover mental health care?
questions.reference: Yes: behavioral health services including inpatient psychiatric care, outpatient mental health, medication management, evaluation and treatment, and substance use treatment.

turns: Can Medicaid help pay medical bills from before I applied?
questions.reference: Possibly: bills up to 10 days before the application date, or up to 3 months before for people requesting long-term care services.

turns: Who can get Med-QUEST?
questions.reference: Hawai'i residents in groups including children, pregnant women, parents and caretakers, adults 19-64, and aged, blind or disabled people. The best way to find out is to apply.

turns: Do pregnant women qualify for Med-QUEST?
questions.reference: Pregnant women are a covered group, with a higher income limit than most adults. Apply to find out.

turns: I'm 70. Is there a limit on savings to qualify?
questions.reference: For people 65 and over, blind or disabled: assets up to $2,000 for one person or $3,000 for two. Over the income limit, the Medically Needy Spenddown program may help.

turns: I got a letter saying my Med-QUEST coverage ended. What should I do?
questions.reference: If you forgot to renew: within 90 days complete the renewal, after 90 days reapply. If it was a mistake: file an appeal. If you no longer qualify: the ACA marketplace.

turns: My application was denied. How do I appeal?
questions.reference: Request an informal review with the eligibility worker or an administrative hearing, in person, by phone, by mail or electronically, within 90 calendar days of the notice.

turns: I have both Medicare and Medicaid. Can I join a dual special needs plan?
questions.reference: Yes, but since January 1, 2026 people newly enrolling can only join the FIDE SNP offered by the same company as their QUEST Integration plan; HIDE SNPs take no new members.

turns: My income is a little over the limit but I have big medical bills. Is there any way to still get help?
questions.reference: Possibly: the Medically Needy Spenddown program can help people over the income limit whose medical expenses are higher than a set spenddown amount (for aged, blind, disabled people, children and pregnant women). Apply to find out.
